items_missed: Never explicitly asked for or confirmed the customer's name during the call itself (used 'miss Lauren' once near the end, likely pulled from caller ID/prior contact rather than asked)
No 'how are you today?' personal check-in — went straight from the greeting into the customer's request
No agenda statement setting expectations for the call, and no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation before diving in
Never confirmed a specific address or zip code for either the loveseat delivery or the sofa relocation
Never asked about stairs/floors at either location
Never asked about special considerations like narrow hallways or tight turns
Never asked about access concerns — parking, HOA restrictions, or elevator access
Never used the 'pricing is super simple' opener before quoting the rate
Quoted a flat $480 minimum but never broke it down into an hourly per-mover rate or mentioned day-of-week tiers
Never covered what's included in the rate — gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads/bands, tools
Never mentioned disassembly/reassembly is included
Meet Your Mover program never mentioned
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned
No 'no hidden fees' pitch — no mention of no credit card fee, no transportation fee, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fee
Never mentioned the 15-minute prorated billing increments after the 2.5-hour minimum
No sense-check ('does that make sense?') after explaining how the clock works
Never gave a typical time range for a job like this, nor stated how many movers/trucks would be sent
No equivalents (e.g. school-bus size comparisons) or walk-distance factor used to help her visualize the job
No deposit required was never explicitly stated
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' — the call ended once she said she'd call back
Never gave office hours or a specific way to reach the team
Used the customer's name only once ('miss Lauren') — short of the 3+ mentions needed
A few stumbled, repetitive moments (e.g. re-asking if she was in Farmers Branch right after she'd already said Dallas) took away from a clean, efficient delivery
60 cents/lb baseline valuation coverage never mentioned alongside the No Worries $2,000 damage coverage
No explicit budget-conscious framing offered despite the customer's clear cost/time-consciousness about the 2.5-hour minimum
top_strength: Chauny repeatedly and clearly explained that billable time only starts once the crew arrives and opens the contract, directly resolving Lauren's core worry about paying for drive time or traffic — exactly why she left the call reassured and thanking him multiple times.
coaching_note: This was a quick 2-item furniture job, so several full-move sections (Save Your Ass prep speech, home-size probing, packing/boxes) genuinely didn't apply and auto-earned their points. But the core fundamentals still got skipped even on a short call: no agenda statement, no hourly-rate/what's-included breakdown, no Meet Your Mover or On-Time Guarantee, and no 'any other questions'/hours-of-operation close. Build the same discovery-to-pitch-to-close shape into short calls too, just condensed.
phone_presence_notes: Chauny stayed warm and reassuring across repeated questions ('Absolutely,' 'no ma'am, you don't pay until we get to you,' 'you're so welcome'), and the customer ended the call clearly satisfied and thankful, though a few stumbled/repetitive lines kept it just short of outstanding.
